chunks.section_title: Section 12-01: Rules Applying to Text of Resolution
chunks.subsection_title: Section 12-01: Rules Applying to Text of Resolution
chunks.text:
Section 12-01: Rules Applying to Text of Resolution
Section 12-01: Rules Applying to Text of Resolution

**Source:** NYC Department of City Planning — zr.planning.nyc.gov  
**Last Amended:** 2/2/2011  
**Retrieved:** March 2026

The following rules of construction apply to the text of this Resolution:

(a) The particular shall control the general.

(b) In case of any difference of meaning or implication between the text of this Resolution and any caption, illustration, summary table or illustrative table, the text shall control.

(c) The word "shall" is always mandatory and not discretionary. The word "may" is permissive.

(d) Words used in the present tense shall include the future; and words used in the singular number shall include the plural, and the plural the singular, unless the context clearly indicates the contrary.

(e) A "building" or "structure" includes any part thereof. The terms **residential building**, **commercial building** and **community facility building** shall refer to an entire **building** used exclusively for such **use**.

(f) The phrase "used for" includes "arranged for", "designed for", "intended for", "maintained for", or "occupied for".

(g) The word "person" includes an individual, a corporation, a partnership, an incorporated association or any other similar entity.

(h) Unless the context clearly indicates the contrary, where a regulation involves two or more items, conditions, provisions, or events connected by the conjunction "and", "or" or "either...or", the conjunction shall be interpreted as follows:
  1. "and" indicates that all the connected items, conditions, provisions or events shall apply;
  2. "or" indicates that the connected items, conditions, provisions or events may apply singly or in any combination; and
  3. "either...or" indicates that the connected items, conditions, provisions or events shall apply singly but not in combination.

(i) The word "includes" shall not limit a term to the specified examples, but is intended to extend its meaning to all other instances or circumstances of like kind or character.

(j) References within a Section or cross-references to a Section numbered with four digits shall include all following Sections with numbers whose first four digits are identical with such Section number, but references or cross-references to a Section numbered with five digits shall refer only to such specific five-digit Section.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 12-02: Rules for Interpretation of District Designations
chunks.subsection_title: Section 12-02: Rules for Interpretation of District Designations
chunks.text:
Section 12-02: Rules for Interpretation of District Designations
Section 12-02: Rules for Interpretation of District Designations

**Last Amended:** 2/2/2011

District designations, where applicable, are listed within a ruled bar below the number and title of each section.

When one or more district designations are listed in a section, the specific text of the paragraphs that follow applies to such district or districts.

When a section includes a table and one or more district designations are listed opposite a specific item or number in such table, the item or number applies specifically to that district or districts only.

When no district designations are listed for a specific section, the provisions of such section shall be construed to apply to all districts under consideration in the Article in which the section appears or, if specified, only to those districts referred to directly within the section itself. For this purpose, Article II applies to all Residence Districts, Article III applies to all Commercial Districts, and Article IV applies to all Manufacturing Districts. All other articles apply to all districts, unless otherwise provided.

chunks.section_title: Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
chunks.text:
Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
abut, or abutting

**Last Amended:** 2/2/2011

"Abut" is to be in contact with or join at the edge or border. "Abutting" **buildings** are **buildings** that are in contact with one another on the same or another **zoning lot**, except as subject to separations required for seismic load as set forth in the New York City Building Code. A **building** may also **abut** a **lot line**. In addition, for **buildings** existing prior to February 2, 2011, such existing **building** shall be considered **abutting** if it is within six inches of a **lot line** or another **building**.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
chunks.text:
Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
accessory use, or accessory

**Last Amended:** 12/5/2024

An "accessory use":

(a) is a **use** conducted on the same **zoning lot** as the principal **use** to which it is related (whether located within the same or an **accessory building or other structure**, or as an **accessory use** of land), except that, where specifically provided in the applicable district regulations or elsewhere in this Resolution, **accessory** docks, off-street parking or off-street loading need not be located on the same **zoning lot**; and

(b) is a **use** which is clearly incidental to, and customarily found in connection with, such principal **use**; and

(c) is either in the same ownership as such principal **use**, or is operated and maintained substantially for the benefit or convenience of the owners, occupants, employees, customers, or visitors of such principal **use**.

Permitted accessory uses include, but are not limited to:
- Swimming pools accessory to Use Group II, provided the edge of the pool is located not less than five feet from any **lot line**, except that such minimum distance may be not less than three feet from any **side lot line** in the case of lots less than 25 feet in width, with screening requirements applied.
- **Accessory** mechanical equipment, including solar or wind energy systems and generators.
- **Home occupations**.
- Domestic storage in a barn, shed, tool room, or similar **building or other structure**.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
chunks.text:
Section 12-10 (Excerpt): Selected Definitions
zoning lot

**Last Amended:** 2/2/2011

A "zoning lot" is either:

(a) a **lot of record** existing on or before December 15, 1961, or a **lot of record** existing on the effective date of applicable district regulations if such regulations were adopted after December 15, 1961; or

(b) a tract of land, either unsubdivided or consisting of two or more contiguous **lots of record**, located within a single **block**, which on the effective date of applicable district regulations, or at any time thereafter, was in single ownership.

For the purposes of **zoning lot** coverage calculations, a **zoning lot** may not be split by a **district** boundary.

chunks.section_title: Section 23-34: Rear Yard and Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements
chunks.text:
Section 23-34: Rear Yard and Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements
23-342: Rear Yard Requirements

**Applicable Districts:** R1 through R10

In all districts, as indicated, a **rear yard** shall be provided at every required **rear lot line** of a **zoning lot**, except as otherwise provided in Sections 23-341 (Permitted obstructions in required rear yards or rear yard equivalents) and 23-344 (Additional rear yard modifications).

The minimum required **rear yard** depth shall be:

| District | Minimum Rear Yard Depth |
|---|---|
| R1 through R5 | 30 feet |
| R6 through R10 | 30 feet |

For corner lots in any Residence District, no rear yard shall be required.

For through lots in any Residence District, each **street** frontage shall be subject to front yard requirements and no rear yard shall be required; however, where a through lot is also a corner lot, the lot shall be subject to both front yard and corner lot regulations.

In R1 through R5 Districts, for lots less than 95 feet in depth, the **rear yard** shall not be less than 20 feet.

**Note:** Permitted obstructions that may be placed in required rear yards — including certain accessory structures, mechanical equipment, and open recreational space elements — are governed by Section 23-341, not this Section. A reader relying solely on Section 23-342 without consulting Section 23-341 will have an incomplete picture of what is permissible in the rear yard.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 23-34: Rear Yard and Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements
chunks.text:
Section 23-34: Rear Yard and Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements
23-343: Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements

Where a **zoning lot** does not have a **rear lot line** as defined in this Resolution, a **rear yard equivalent** shall be provided. The **rear yard equivalent** shall comply with the same minimum depth requirements as specified in Section 23-342.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 23-34: Rear Yard and Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements
chunks.text:
Section 23-34: Rear Yard and Rear Yard Equivalent Requirements
23-344: Additional Rear Yard Modifications

The **rear yard** requirement may be modified under certain conditions, including:

(a) Where the **Board of Standards and Appeals** grants a variance pursuant to Article VII.

(b) For developments on **zoning lots** that are predominantly occupied by existing buildings, certain alternative rear yard depths may apply as set forth in Section 23-711 (Predominantly Built-up Areas).

(c) In the Special Purpose Districts established under Articles VIII through XIV, alternative rear yard requirements may supersede those set forth in this Section; the applicable Special Purpose District regulations shall control.

chunks.section_title: Section 23-341: Permitted Obstructions in Required Rear Yards or Rear Yard Equivalents
chunks.subsection_title: Section 23-341: Permitted Obstructions in Required Rear Yards or Rear Yard Equivalents
chunks.text:
Section 23-341: Permitted Obstructions in Required Rear Yards or Rear Yard Equivalents
Section 23-341: Permitted Obstructions in Required Rear Yards or Rear Yard Equivalents

**Source:** NYC Department of City Planning — zr.planning.nyc.gov  
**Last Amended:** 11/10/2022  
**Retrieved:** March 2026

---

In all Residence Districts, the following shall not be considered obstructions when located in a required **rear yard** or **rear yard equivalent**:

(a) **Fences or walls** not exceeding six feet in height as measured from natural grade.

(b) **Arbors or trellises**.

(c) **Recreational and play equipment**, including children's play apparatus, sandboxes, swimming pools (above-ground), and similar structures, provided that no such structure shall exceed a height of six feet as measured from natural grade.

(d) **Statuary, flagpoles**, or similar ornamental features not exceeding 15 feet in height.

(e) **Solar energy systems**, including solar panels mounted on, or not more than 18 inches above, the roof of a structure located in the rear yard, provided such structure is itself a permitted obstruction.

(f) **Planting, including trees**, shrubbery, and ground cover.

(g) **Accessory buildings or other structures** not exceeding 10 feet in height as measured from natural grade, provided that the total **floor area** of all such structures does not exceed 80 square feet, and provided that such structures are set back at least four feet from the **rear lot line** and from each **side lot line**.

**Important limitation:** Air conditioning units, mechanical equipment serving the principal building, and emergency generators are NOT listed as permitted obstructions in rear yards under this Section. Such equipment shall comply with the screening requirements of Section 26-50. Where a conflict exists between this Section and any Special Purpose District regulation, the Special Purpose District regulation shall control (see Section 12-01(a): the particular shall control the general).

chunks.section_title: Section 23-32: Front Yard Requirements
chunks.subsection_title: 23-321: Basic Front Yard Requirements in R1 Through R5 Districts

Section 23-32: Front Yard Requirements
23-321: Basic Front Yard Requirements in R1 Through R5 Districts

In all R1 through R5 Districts, a **front yard** shall be provided for every **zoning lot** and shall be not less than the depth specified in the following table, except as otherwise provided in Sections 23-311 (Permitted obstructions in all yards, courts and open areas) and 23-312 (Additional permitted obstructions generally permitted in all yards).

| District | Minimum Front Yard Depth |
|---|---|
| R1 | 20 feet |
| R2 | 20 feet |
| R3 | 15 feet |
| R3A | 15 feet |
| R3X | 20 feet |
| R4 | 10 feet |
| R4A | 20 feet |
| R4B | 10 feet |
| R5 | 10 feet |
| R5A | 20 feet |
| R5B | 15 feet |
| R5D | 10 feet |

**Contextual front yard modification:** Where 40 percent or more of the lots within 150 feet on either side of the **zoning lot** and on the same side of the **street**, within the same **block**, are occupied by **buildings** with front yards of less than the depth required by this Section, the minimum required front yard depth may be the average of the two such front yards nearest to each side of the **zoning lot** in question, but in no event less than 8 feet.

**Planting requirement:** In all R1 through R5 Districts, at least 50 percent of the area of any required front yard shall be planted and maintained with **landscaped** ground cover or other plantings, pursuant to Section 23-613 (Front yard planting requirements).

chunks.section_title: Section 23-32: Front Yard Requirements
chunks.subsection_title: 23-322: Front Yard Requirements for R6 Through R12 Districts
chunks.text:
Section 23-32: Front Yard Requirements
23-322: Front Yard Requirements for R6 Through R12 Districts

In R6 through R12 Districts, no minimum **front yard** depth is required as a general rule; however, **street wall** location requirements and setback provisions set forth in Section 23-431 (Street wall location requirements) and Section 23-433 (Standard setback regulations) shall apply where indicated.

chunks.section_title: Section 23-311: Permitted Obstructions in All Yards, Courts and Open Areas
chunks.subsection_title: Section 23-311: Permitted Obstructions in All Yards, Courts and Open Areas
chunks.text:
Section 23-311: Permitted Obstructions in All Yards, Courts and Open Areas
Section 23-311: Permitted Obstructions in All Yards, Courts and Open Areas

**Source:** NYC Department of City Planning — zr.planning.nyc.gov  
**Last Amended:** 11/10/2022  
**Retrieved:** March 2026

---

In all districts, the following shall not be considered obstructions and may penetrate any **yard**, **court**, or other required open area:

(a) **Awnings and canopies**, provided that they are not more than 4 feet deep measured from the exterior face of the building wall, and provided that they do not extend beyond 18 inches from any **lot line**.

(b) **Belt courses, sills, headers, pilasters, cornices, eaves** or **gutters**, provided that such features do not extend more than 2 feet into any **yard**.

(c) **Open fire escapes**, provided that they do not extend more than 3.5 feet into any **yard** and are not located within 15 feet of any **street** or **lot line**, except in the case of lots less than 50 feet in width.

(d) **Handicapped ramps and access features** required by the New York City Building Code or the Americans with Disabilities Act, provided that such ramps do not extend more than 4 feet into any required **front yard**.

(e) **Planters, garden structures** (including pergolas, trellises, and lattice work not exceeding 8 feet in height), provided such structures do not cover more than 25 percent of the open yard area.

(f) **Driveways and walkways** at grade, in any **side** or **rear yard**, providing access to a **street** or to an **accessory** off-street parking space.

(g) **Steps** (including stoops) leading to the entrance of a **building**, provided that they do not occupy more than 30 square feet of required **front yard** area.

(h) **Heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment** (condensers and similar elements), provided that such equipment does not extend more than 2 feet into any **rear yard** and is not located within any **front yard**. Such equipment shall comply with the noise and screening provisions of Section 26-50.

**Note on scope:** This Section governs permitted obstructions in *all* yards. Additional permitted obstructions specific to rear yards are set forth in Section 23-341. Where a feature is listed in both sections, the more permissive provision applies.

chunks.section_title: What is an (E) Designation?
chunks.text:
What is an (E) Designation?
What is an (E) Designation?

An **(E) designation** is an environmental requirement placed on a **zoning lot** as part of a zoning map amendment or other CEQR action. The designation identifies a site that may have potential hazardous materials, air quality, or noise concerns that must be addressed before a building permit can be issued.

There are three types of (E) designations:
- **(E) Hazardous Materials** — the lot may contain soil or groundwater contamination requiring investigation and potentially remediation before development.
- **(E) Air Quality** — development on the lot must incorporate specific air quality mitigation measures (e.g., HVAC intake placement, building materials).
- **(E) Noise** — development must achieve specified interior noise attenuation levels.

A single lot may carry multiple (E) designation types simultaneously.

---

chunks.section_title: How to Use This Table
chunks.text:
How to Use This Table
How to Use This Table

(E) designations are indexed by **CEQR Number** and **Tax Block and Lot** (BBL). The presence of a **Hazardous Materials (E)** designation does not necessarily mean contamination is present — it means an investigation is required. The outcome of such investigation may clear the designation or may require remediation, subject to review by the NYC Mayor's Office of Environmental Remediation (OER).

**Important:** (E) designations attach to the zoning lot as defined in this Resolution and run with the land. They are not automatically removed upon sale or change of ownership. Only formal OER sign-off following a Phase II ESA and any required remediation can lift the designation.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 23-43: Height and Setback Requirements in R6 Through R12 Districts
chunks.text:
Section 23-43: Height and Setback Requirements in R6 Through R12 Districts
23-431: Street Wall Location Requirements

In R6A, R6B, R7A, R7B, R7D, R7X, R8A, R8B, R8X, R9A, R9D, R9X, R10A, and R10X Districts, the **street wall** of any **building** shall be located as follows:

(a) Within 8 feet of the **street line**, except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b) through (d) of this Section;

(b) Where an existing building on the same **zoning lot** has a **street wall** located further from the **street line** than required by paragraph (a), the new **street wall** shall be located no further from the **street line** than such existing **street wall**;

(c) At a **street line** where the **building** contains ground floor retail or other non-residential **uses**, the **street wall** shall be located at the **street line**, or within 2 feet thereof, for a minimum of 70 percent of the **street** frontage.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 23-43: Height and Setback Requirements in R6 Through R12 Districts
chunks.text:
Section 23-43: Height and Setback Requirements in R6 Through R12 Districts
23-432: Height and Setback Requirements

In R6 through R12 Districts, **buildings** shall comply with a base height and setback envelope before a tower or upper portion may rise to the maximum permitted height.

**Base heights** (maximum before setback is required):

| District | Min Base Height | Max Base Height |
|---|---|---|
| R6A | 25 ft | 45 ft |
| R6B | 25 ft | 35 ft |
| R7A | 40 ft | 65 ft |
| R7B | 30 ft | 45 ft |
| R7X | 60 ft | 85 ft |
| R8A | 60 ft | 85 ft |
| R8B | 40 ft | 65 ft |
| R8X | 60 ft | 105 ft |
| R9A | 60 ft | 85 ft |
| R9X | 60 ft | 105 ft |
| R10A | 60 ft | 105 ft |

After the base height is reached, a setback of at least 10 feet from the **street wall** shall be provided before the **building** may rise to its maximum permitted height.

In standard R6, R7, R8, R9, and R10 Districts (non-contextual), the sky exposure plane regulations of Section 23-73 apply in lieu of this table.

---

chunks.section_title: Section 23-43: Height and Setback Requirements in R6 Through R12 Districts
chunks.text:
Section 23-43: Height and Setback Requirements in R6 Through R12 Districts
23-433: Standard Setback Regulations

In R6A, R6B, R7A, R7B, R7D, R7X, R8A, R8B, R8X, R9A, R9D, R9X, R10A, and R10X Districts, above the maximum base height, a setback of at least 10 feet from the **street wall** below shall be provided at all **street** frontages before the **building** may rise to the maximum permitted height for the district.

Where a **building** does not front on a **street**, setback requirements shall be determined by the provisions for **rear yards** and **side yards** applicable to the district.
